label: y as the first token (t=0)
explanation: Fires at step 0 when the first original input token is y, at a near-constant activation (median 1.98 = max; every y-at-t=0 step fires, precision 1.0). It does not fire on y anywhere else in the original phase, at the delimiter, or on other tokens. Residual activations are weak (~0.04-0.08 of max): y at t=1 right after k or c (~1000 dev steps), plus a few copy-phase steps where y is fed back as input (~0.14 of max). The predicate covers 99.8% of activation mass.

issues: Claims mostly check out. Test split: precision 1.0 with 0 false positives, recall 0.937, mass recall 0.998. Dev profile: the feature fires only when in_tok is y, 99.8% of mass is at t=0, it never fires at the delimiter, and the median activation (1.981) equals the max.

The recall gap is one systematic but very weak class: y at t=1 when orig(0) is k or c. The predicate (t==1)&(y)&(orig0 in {k,c}) has precision 1.0 and covers all 1058 dev t=1 activations, but they hold only 0.2% of the mass. Plain y at t=1 has precision 0.06, so the k/c condition is needed.

Minor inaccuracy: the explanation puts the t=1 residual at about 0.04-0.08 of max, but the observed values are about 0.03-0.04. The copy-phase residual is only 49 dev steps (about 0.0% of mass), so it is negligible.
